predictions: evidence/diff-oracle-predictions.json (registered before any contact with the solutions)
verdict: D-1 CONFIRMED, D-2 PRIMARY CONFIRMED, D-3 CONFIRMED for the core family. Mechanically diff-derived predicates achieved PERFECT SEPARATION on the exact material three generations of mind-derived predicates failed on: all nine 92-scoring defective solutions RED, the shipped reference and the altformat valid variant both GREEN — at zero provider calls.

derivation.corpus: 20 deterministic generic-markdown inputs (link runs 1-6, duplication patterns, spread links, three list-marker styles, unicode, long prose, bare URL, block prose, plain control) — domain knowledge, no answer knowledge (tested: no input names any convention)
derivation.pipeline: run before & after on the corpus via a driver built from PUBLIC surface only (buildEditionDoc + the stub's global, both visible in tests/public.test.js); compare emitted streams under 7 generic projections (seq, multiset, uniq, bigrams, joined, count, charset); admit a predicate only if red-on-before, green-on-after AND green-on-altformat
derivation.note_on_filter: the altformat variant killed 40 format-pinning candidates mechanically — the over-constraint failure class that took down 3 of 9 authored checks in the notes-transfer test, handled here with zero judgement

interpretability.run-unique-N::count family (CLEAN WIN): the piece COUNT on a run of adjacent citations captures the PRESENCE of separator material without pinning its identity — comma and middot change the count identically, so the predicate survives the altformat filter while every solution that emits no separator goes red. This is precisely the run-separation behaviour, derived mechanically; no mind in three generations wrote this predicate.
interpretability.list-parens::* family (HONEST FLAG): likely pins the shipped fix's specific (N)-marker normalization beyond what the conventions document requires: the held-out oracle deemed all nine solutions' enum handling acceptable, and the valid-variant pool (n=1, differing ONLY in separator) cannot kill list-behaviour pinning. A richer valid-variant pool would probably retire these. Reported as a measured limitation of a 1-variant filter, not hidden.

what_this_is_and_is_not.is: the first mechanism in this repository that measurably discriminates where minds failed, produced at zero provider calls from git history + a generic corpus + generic projections. The hypothesis 'predicates must come from the diff, not from prose comprehension' now has direct supporting evidence on real material.
is_not: a cross-task result: one fixture, one behaviour family (within-task, like every result on vextrum)
free of input-provisioning dependency: the corpus generator embeds domain knowledge (markdown primitives); a different domain needs a different generator or mined inputs

a complete over-constraint solution: the valid-variant filter is only as strong as the variant pool (see the list-parens flag); real deployments should mine multiple valid variants from history when they exist
wired into the campaign loop yet: the derived suite is not yet a harness check kind consumed by loop arms — that is the next build step

next_steps_zero_calls_first: wire derived predicates into the harness as a check kind (they are exact-match projections: trivially executable, sha-pinned)

shadow-replay generalization: commit mining on real Hermes/Vextrum history (select fix commits, materialize before/after, mine inputs from repo samples/tests), which turns this from a fixture proof into the product mechanism

the decisive NEXT measurement (needs spend approval): a loop arm whose suite is DIFF-DERIVED instead of authored, on a fresh task family — does the loop with mechanical predicates beat vanilla-configured where the authored loop could not?
